title: Choose BizWallet's visual world
question: The roll assigned Pasar Malam Stall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pasar Malam Stall
options.lineage: Malaysian night markets: tarp canopies, tube lights, marker-on-cardboard price cards
options.thesis: Each restaurant gets its own lit stall: its photos under a tube-light strip, every action a bold card hung from the canopy.
options.viewport: Restaurant photo full-bleed under a white light strip; its name on a hanging card; Order / Call staff / Bill as big clipped cards; points as one marker-written card.
options.risk: Turns into costume if marker type and kraft texture spread past the few signs into every label.

raised.raise: One visible cell grid: every card snaps to it, no free-floating boxes.
Three type sizes only; rank comes from weight and case, not size creep.
Dish photos at one fixed scale and crop everywhere, so menus read as a set.
Total palette commitment: tarp blue, canopy red, kraft and ink; nothing else.

options.label: Mamak Order Chit
options.lineage: carbon-copy order pads and table chits at mamak and kopitiam
options.thesis: Every screen is the restaurant's own order pad: table number, items and totals on a chit, stamped PAID when settled.
options.viewport: A chit headed by the restaurant and table number; order, bill and split live on its ruled lines; the next action stamped at the foot.
options.risk: The most familiar paper-receipt look; can feel like admin rather than a treat.

options.label: Rail Line Map
options.thesis: Your visit as a coloured line: Seated, Ordered, Cooking, Ready, Paid are stations you ride through.
options.viewport: A bold route line running down the table page, the current stop lit; actions branch off it as stations.
options.case: Wins clarity for order progress and bill steps; diners don't feel 'restaurant' in it.
options.risk: Restaurant photos fight the diagram; can feel like a transport app.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and departure boards
options.thesis: Your table is a pass: table number and order as segments; the kitchen is a live board that reranks as dishes get ready.
options.viewport: A pass with TABLE A5 huge and segments for order, bill and points; below, a live board of your dishes.
options.case: Strong for live status and splitting; weak on feeling like a restaurant.
options.risk: Travel metaphor can feel cold for a meal.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid type over a cell grid.
options.case: Diners don't recognise it; it would bury the restaurant.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.case: Too foreign to the table moment; hurts clarity.
options.kept: Few type sizes, rank by weight and case.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: Cream-and-serif rut; nothing to do with a mamak.
options.kept: Dish photos at one fixed scale.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Black and white data fields only.
options.case: Hostile to diners and to restaurant photos.

canonCard.label: The food-app standard
canonCard.thesis: What Grab, foodpanda and every QR-ordering app ship, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Photo header, pill actions, list sections; the arrangement diners already expect.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other ordering app by design.
